title: Quarterly runway & sprint handoff for Hosted API + Model Catalog with contingency lanes
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Objective: Prepare a prescriptive, handoff-ready quarterly runway and sprint playbook that aligns Hosted API priorities with the Model Catalog cadence. This ticket creates the canonical artifact that PMs, Eng leads, Design, and SREs will use for sprint-by-sprint execution, canary scheduling, and contingency activation.

Scope: Hosted API feature launches (streaming improvements, structured output beta), model catalog rotations (variant gating, deprecation windows), canary windows and rollback criteria, observability dashboards to track OKR signals (latency P50/P95, cost per token, model quality regressions), and a contingency lane mapping for capacity/risk events.

Deliverables:
- Quarterly Runway Playbook (Confluence): milestones, owner matrix, canary calendar, rollback playbook, communication templates.
- Sprint Handoff Checklist (Drive): per-sprint acceptance gates, test prompts, eval set links, QA sign-off template.
- Risk Matrix & Contingency Lanes (internal doc): triggers to invoke fallback routing to cheaper/compatible model variants, cross-region failover steps.
- Dashboard snapshots: OKR healthboard (latency/cost/quality) + traffic forecasts for model fleet.

Key tradeoffs noted during scoping:
- Conservative rotation window preserves SLA but delays model upgrades; aggressive rotation reduces technical debt but increases short-term regression risk. We propose a hybrid cadence: major model swaps every 8 weeks with a 2-week canary and a 2-week observation buffer.
- Batching/cache knobs that reduce cost may worsen tail latency for interactive workloads; include per-route recommended profiles rather than global defaults.

Links to artifacts:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/Quarterly+Runway+Playbook+Q2-2026
- Sprint checklist (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/hosted/q2-runway-sprint-checklist
- Eval harness & prompts (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/evals/hosted-model-eval-sets
- Draft dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/okrs/hosted-model-fleet
- Initial PR for playbook templates: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1842

Stakeholders: Priya Nair (PM Lead), Diego Alvarez (Product Owner), Liam O'Connor (Eng Lead - Serving), Tasha Green (SRE), Arjun Patel (Research/Model Ops), Hannah Li (Design).
acceptance_criteria: Confluence runway document is published and reviewed by PM/Eng/SRE/Design
Sprint handoff checklist exists and is linked in the repo with a template PR
Canary calendar created and approved; calendar includes rollback owner and SLA impact estimate
Dashboard snapshots show baseline metrics and a plan to surface regressions to oncall
Contingency lanes documented with play-by-play runbooks and a communication template
